approval_trigger: Two independent triggers, both supported by internal/config as written. (1) approvals.rules[0] is {match: {profile: approval-gated}, action: require_approval}: every request naming profile approval-gated parks pending_approval, which is what S065-S071 use. (2) The catalog entries s3.write-prefix and lambda.invoke set requires_approval: true, so they park on ANY profile including default, which is what S072 uses. guardrails.first_use_approval is false, so no first-use approvals fire. Approve or deny over the admin unix socket: taskgrant approve --config <config_path> --note '...' <grant_id> (and taskgrant deny ...). Verified end to end: request -> pending_approval -> approve -> get_grant returns active with credentials exactly once.
s077_narrow: What the code enforces per agent is the PROFILE allowlist, so agent-077 is configured with profiles [narrow] and default_profile narrow: list_capabilities as agent-077 returns profiles == ["narrow"] and default_profile == "narrow", while every other agent returns the four-profile list. That half of S077 is real and assertable. The other half (only logs.read visible) is NOT achievable without editing product source: capability visibility is a per-capability field in the catalog YAML (Capability.Agents, internal/synth/catalog/catalog.go, honored by Snapshot.ForAgent and Broker.ListCapabilities), and the shipped examples/catalog sets no agents: list on any entry, so all seven capabilities are visible to every agent. Observed: agent-077 sees [dynamodb.query, lambda.invoke, logs.read, s3.read-prefix, s3.write-prefix, sqs.consume, sqs.produce]. S077 should therefore assert profile filtering plus the fact that entries are listed (not disabled), and record the capability-visibility half as a documented harness limitation, not a broker failure.

mcp_call_usage.output: default prints {"tool":..., "is_error":..., "structured_content":{...}, "content":[...]}; --raw prints only the structured content

exit_codes.0: the server returned a tool result, INCLUDING denials, clarifications, and tool-level errors (those are normal results)
exit_codes.1: usage or argument error (bad flags, unreadable token file, malformed --args JSON)
exit_codes.2: transport, auth, or session failure (broker unreachable, 401 on an invalid or expired bearer)
exit_codes.3: the call failed at the JSON-RPC protocol level

durations.effective_rule: effective = min(request, capability cap 900, profile cap, global cap 3600), floor 900. Because every catalog entry caps at 900, every successful mint in this harness lands on 900 seconds no matter what the request or profile allows. Observed: request 3600 on profile default (cap 1800) granted 900.

audit.flag_order: the CLI uses the Go flag package, which stops at the first positional argument: put every flag BEFORE the grant id. 'audit show <id> --json' silently fails; 'audit show --json <id>' is correct.
audit.note: the audit CLI opens the SQLite decision log directly (WAL, concurrent readers), so it works while the broker runs

notes: LocalStack STS returns real session credentials but does NOT enforce the session policy: a minted credential can do more against LocalStack than the policy allows. Prove scope from the policy document (explain_grant.policy_json, audit record) and use minted credentials only to prove the mint path is real (sts get-caller-identity returns an assumed-role ARN of the profile role).

Every catalog entry caps max_duration_seconds at 900, so every mint clamps to 900 seconds regardless of the profile cap (1800) or the requested value. The duration family should assert the min() chain, not a 1800 grant.

s3.write-prefix and lambda.invoke carry requires_approval: true in examples/catalog, so scenarios S003 and S008 park pending_approval on the default profile before any mint. That is correct broker behavior; reach active by approving over the admin socket, and say so in the evidence.

No synth.llm block is configured (deterministic rules matcher only, as the corpus requires). Observed baseline for the keyword-match family: request_grant with free text and no capabilities hints, for example 'download the invoice files from the invoices bucket, prefix 2026/', returns status denied with denial_code NEEDS_STRUCTURED_HINTS rather than needs_clarification with candidates. Record what you observe and judge it against your family's expect text; do not assume either outcome.

Hostile or non-allowlisted parameter values surface as status needs_clarification with clarification.code INVALID_PARAM (or MISSING_PARAM) plus the exact param, expected shape, and allowlist examples, not as status denied. Observed with bucket acme-secret-data. No STS call happens on that path.
S077 capability-visibility limitation: see s077_narrow above.

No broker restart helper is provided and scenario agents must not restart the broker (the fleet shares one long-lived process). The restart sub-checks of S063 and S071 are therefore skipped by design; report the rest of those scenarios normally and note the skipped sub-check.
